outputs.explanation: This is a scatter plot in which each marker is one of the 141 individual samples; individual points are the data itself, and the marginal histograms summarize the same raw individual measurements. No overlay is needed.
Scatter plot showing one point per cell-line/reporter with error bars (mean ± s.d.); scatter plots are exempt from the individual-points requirement per the check's plot-type rules.
These are line/density (distribution) plots, which are exempt from requiring overlaid individual points.
Box plots already display the data distribution and are exempt; additionally, individual data points (dots for Per2-Luc and Bmal1-Luc) are visibly overlaid on the boxes in the figure.

Polar histograms depict the distribution of phase-difference values (analogous to a histogram/violin showing distribution shape) and are exempt from requiring an additional overlay of individual points.
Same reasoning as panel E: a polar histogram displaying distribution shape across subtypes, exempt from needing individual point overlays.

This panel shows an illustrative example fit (raw trace, fitted curve, and sketched decay envelope) to explain the fitting procedure rather than aggregated/summary data across samples, so the individual-points requirement does not apply.

Scatter plot in which each marker is one of the 117 individual samples (with error bars reflecting fit uncertainty for that sample, not averaging across replicates); individual points are already the data shown.
